title: Strict reduction of completed extension by zero
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $I\subset A$ a finitely generated ideal, $A/I$ additive torsion, and $P_n=A/I^n$ finite as a set (so a finite commutative ring) and perfect over $A$ for every $n\geq1$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-coefficient-datum]. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion of schemes [def-weil-open-immersion]. Work on the small pro-etale sites, with constant $A$-module sheaves and their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $J_j$ for the exact module extension by zero along the localized site, also applied termwise to strict inverse sequences and complexes [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact, lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Put $\mathcal T_T=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{op},\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A_T))$ [def-weil-inverse-system], and use the diagram-site model [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. Define the strict reduction functor $\mathcal R_T(M)=\Delta M\otimes^L_{\Delta\underline A_T}(\underline{P_n}_T)_n$, computed on one flat-term K-flat representative [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Let $C_TM=R\lim\mathcal R_T(M)$ be completion with its specified unit $\eta_M:M\to C_TM$ [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], and put $J_j^cK=C_X(J_jK)$.

Extension by zero sends flat-term K-flat complexes to flat-term K-flat complexes. The tensor projection comparison gives a natural isomorphism of actual derived strict towers
$$\mathcal R_X(J_jK)\xrightarrow{\sim}J_j\mathcal R_U(K).$$
For every $K\in D(U,A)$, the morphism $\mathcal R_X(\eta_{J_jK})$ is invertible, and its inverse followed by this tensor comparison defines
$$q_{j,K}:\mathcal R_X(J_j^cK)\xrightarrow{\sim}J_j\mathcal R_U(K),\qquad q_{j,K}\,\mathcal R_X(\eta_{J_jK})=q^{\rm tens}_{j,K}.$$
At each $n$, its inverse is the reduction of the completion unit and its forward map is the adjoint of the $n$-th limit projection; in particular $(J_j^cK)\otimes_A^LP_n\cong J_j(K\otimes_A^LP_n)$. These statements are natural in $K$ and respect every quotient transition before taking $R\lim$. Moreover $J_j^cK$ is complete and its completion presentation gives the specified natural isomorphism $J_j^cK\cong R\lim(J_j\mathcal R_UK)$. If the reductions of $K$ have bounded-below etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], those of $J_j^cK$ have the extension-by-zero witnesses through [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]. No completeness of ordinary $J_jK$, and no commutation of ordinary $J_j$ with inverse limits, is asserted.

source.place: Proof Steps 1–2, integral open factor: the extension-by-zero identification used in the compactification formula; original split Step 3, paragraphs beginning “For the integral open factor” and “The completion unit”; agent-stated strict-diagram prerequisite of the blueprint argument; ingredient sources are Stacks proetale.tex, Tags 099M (lemma-naive-completion), 099N (lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case), and sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), not a verbatim assertion of one tag.

proof.text: Choose a K-flat representative P→K with flat terms using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Under [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] (applied with the rings A and P_n), U_proet is the localization X_proet/U and A_X|_U=A_U, (P_n)_X|_U=(P_n)_U, so J_j is the localized-site extension by zero of [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Exactness of localized-site extension by zero gives a quasi-isomorphism J_jP→J_jK. The ringed-slice tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor], applied with the coefficient sheaf (P_n)_X, identifies J_jP⊗_{A_X}(P_n)_X with J_j(P⊗_{A_U}(P_n)_U). For a flat O_U-module G the functor F↦(J_jG)⊗F≅J_j(G⊗F|_U) is exact, so J_jG is flat. J_j is a left adjoint, so it commutes with the direct sums forming total tensor complexes; since restriction is exact and J_j is exact, tensoring J_jP with any acyclic A_X-complex is the extension by zero of the corresponding acyclic tensor on U. Thus J_jP is again K-flat with flat terms in the sense of [def-pc-kflat-complex], and it computes all derived reductions of J_jK.

source.place: Proof Step 1, integral open factor: extension by zero and tensor model

proof.text: Use the diagram-site realization [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization] to regard the levelwise comparisons as morphisms of strict towers. For every n the preceding tensor comparison gives (J_jK)⊗^L_A P_n ≅ J_j(K⊗^L_A P_n). On a flat-term model it sends a pure tensor to the same extension-by-zero generator, so it commutes with the quotient maps P_{n+1}→P_n. The definition of inverse systems [def-weil-inverse-system] then makes these level maps a natural isomorphism of actual derived strict towers, denoted q^{tens}_{j,K}: R_X(J_jK)≅J_jR_U(K).

source.place: Proof Step 1, strict diagram and quotient-transition compatibility

proof.text: Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-adic-completion-reduction] to the object J_jK on X. Its hypotheses are exactly the Noetherian complete-coefficient datum and perfect finite quotients in the statement, and no completeness hypothesis on J_jK is required. Writing C_X(J_jK)=R lim_n R_X(J_jK) [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction], it states that the adjoint a_n of each limit projection p_n is an isomorphism C_X(J_jK)⊗^L_A P_n→(J_jK)⊗^L_A P_n. By [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction] the completion unit η_{J_jK} is the completion map J_jK→R lim_n R_X(J_jK), so p_n∘η_{J_jK} is the canonical reduction J_jK→(J_jK)⊗^L_A P_n, whose adjoint is the identity. Naturality of the scalar-extension adjunction therefore gives a_n∘R_X(η_{J_jK})_n=a_{n}∘(η_{J_jK}⊗^L P_n)=id; as a_n is invertible, the n-th component of R_X(η_{J_jK}) is the isomorphism a_n^{-1}. Exactness in the tower category is levelwise [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], so the cone of R_X(η_{J_jK}) is acyclic and R_X(η_{J_jK}) is invertible as a morphism of derived strict towers.

source.place: Statement and proof: finite reduction of the derived completion tower

proof.text: Define q_{j,K} as the composite of the inverse of R_X(η_{J_jK}) with q^{tens}_{j,K}. Both factors are natural in K, so q_{j,K} is natural and is an isomorphism. By its definition, q_{j,K}∘R_X(η_{J_jK})=q^{tens}_{j,K}. The inverse at level n is the finite reduction of the completion unit, while the forward map is the adjoint of the n-th limit projection, exactly as in the completion-reduction lemma and the specified unit of [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction].

source.place: Original split Step 3, paragraph beginning The completion unit

proof.text: Evaluating q_{j,K} at n gives (J_j^cK)⊗^L_A P_n≅J_j(K⊗^L_A P_n), and Step 2 shows that these identifications commute with every quotient transition before R lim [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. For witnesses this iso is needed in D(X_proet,P_n): the inverse of the level-n reduced unit is the adjoint a_n, an isomorphism in D(X_proet,P_n) by [lemma-weil-pbc-adic-completion-reduction], and the level-n tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor] with F=(P_n)_X is (P_n)_X-linear, by its naturality in F applied to the scalar endomorphisms of (P_n)_X. Since P_n is a finite commutative ring, J_j on P_n-modules is the functor j_!^{proet} of [def-weil-extension-by-zero] (same sheafified extension-by-zero presheaf on X_proet/U). Let K_n have the witness (L_n,α_n), L_n∈D^+(U_et,P_n). Apply [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] termwise to a bounded-below complex representing L_n; the functors ν^* (exact: a left adjoint preserving finite limits on the underlying sheaves [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]), j_!^{et} [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] and j_!^{proet} [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero] are exact and applied degreewise, so the termwise natural isomorphism is an isomorphism ν_X^*(j_!^{et}L_n)≅j_!^{proet}ν_U^*L_n in D^+(X_proet,P_n). Composing with j_!^{proet}(α_n) and the level-n isomorphism above gives ν_X^*(j_!^{et}L_n)≅(J_j^cK)⊗^L_A P_n, so (j_!^{et}L_n, this composite) is the required bounded-below extension-by-zero witness for the n-th reduction of J_j^cK. No transitions between the witnesses are asserted.

source.place: Comparison of etale and pro-etale extension by zero

proof.text: By the defining formula for completion in [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction], J_j^cK=C_X(J_jK) is complete and is canonically R lim_n R_X(J_jK). Substituting the strict-tower isomorphism q^{tens}_{j,K} from Step 2 gives the specified natural presentation J_j^cK≅R lim_n(J_jR_UK). This uses only the derived limit of the strict reduction tower; it does not identify J_j(R lim_n R_UK) with R lim_n(J_jR_UK), so no commutation of ordinary J_j with inverse limits is asserted.

source.place: Proof Steps 1–2, integral open factor: completion presentation

proof.text: All constructions above are induced by functorial K-flat replacement, the natural extension/tensor comparison, the quotient maps, and the completion unit. Therefore they respect morphisms of K and all tower transitions. The identity and zero-stalk descriptions of extension by zero are preserved levelwise, and the assertions are unchanged for the edge cases j=id and K=0. The final qualification follows from the construction in Step 6 and is part of the claimed typing.

(3) E5/C1: Step 5 applied a sheaf-level comparison to D^+ complexes and gave no P_n-linear level isomorphism. It now uses exactness of nu^*, j_!^et and j_!^proet, the P_n-linear isomorphism from the reduction lemma and the tensor comparison, the identification of J_j with def-weil-extension-by-zero, and composition with j_!(alpha_n).
